note: Controlled stress tests with the PRODUCTION model on PaySim strict-test rows. They describe model behaviour under input changes. They do NOT demonstrate robustness; every row that scores >= 0.5 after a change is simply an observation.

scenarios.observation: 99.7% of sampled fraud rows score >= 0.5; 0.0% of sampled legitimate TRANSFER/CASH_OUT rows score >= 0.5.

scenarios.input_modification: split each fraud amount into 2 equal consecutive transfers from the same account, consistent balances, same step
scenarios.observation: Only the final part empties the account; earlier parts leave a residual balance.
scenarios.limitation: Same-step history is ignored by the strict point-in-time policy, so history features cannot help here.

scenarios.scenario: gradual / repeated smaller transfers x4 (one per step)
scenarios.input_modification: same as splitting but one part per consecutive step so sender history exists
scenarios.observation: History features exist for later parts, but they were inert in training (SHAP 0).
scenarios.limitation: The model has no velocity feature; the user_* history features were effectively constant in training.

scenarios.scenario: recipient change: new recipient account (zero balances)
scenarios.input_modification: change nameDest (no model feature) and/or destination balances
scenarios.observation: The model has no recipient-identity feature; only the destination balance features respond.
scenarios.limitation: Recipient identity is invisible to the XGBoost model; only network signals could see it.

scenarios.input_modification: set type=TRANSFER, all other fields unchanged
scenarios.observation: Changes the five one-hot type features only.
scenarios.limitation: PaySim fraud only occurs as TRANSFER/CASH_OUT, so other types are out-of-distribution for fraud.

scenarios.scenario: balance manipulation: sender new balance +1 (account not fully emptied)
scenarios.observation: Shows how strongly the model relies on exact balance consistency (known PaySim shortcut).
scenarios.limitation: This is an input the sender cannot freely control in a real system; it is a diagnostic, not a threat model.
